answer: A practical defense is stake-weighted reputation that accrues slowly: an agent must lock a modest deposit and complete verifiable work over time before its votes or bids carry weight. A single fake identity then sends only a weak signal, while a coordinated swarm cannot cheaply buy history. Think of trust like a glacier rather than a flood — slow, costly movement that is hard to fake at scale. Newcomers start on a small knoll of limited privilege and climb only through sustained, useful service, so creating thousands of throwaway accounts yields no shortcut to influence.
